core_summary: Motion is defined as a change in position of an object over time relative to a reference frame. Speed measures how fast an object moves: Speed = Distance / Time (SI unit: m/s, practical unit: km/h). Motion is classified as Uniform (constant speed along a straight line covering equal distances in equal time intervals) or Non-uniform (changing speed). Time measurement evolved from natural periodic phenomena (sun, moon phases) to mechanical simple pendulums and quartz crystal oscillators. Distance-Time graphs visually depict motion dynamics.
key_concepts: To measure and verify the constancy of a simple pendulum's time period.

key_terms.definition: The time taken by a pendulum or oscillating system to complete one full back-and-forth oscillation.

key_takeaways: The time period of a simple pendulum depends strictly on string length and gravitational acceleration, independent of bob mass.
